spoilage detection: A case study on bananas
Rajini Ma,*, Persis Voolab
a Department of CSE, Government Degree College, Ravulapalem, A.P, India
b Department of CSE, Adikavi Nannaya University, Rajahmundry, A.P, India
ARTICLE INFO
Keywords:
Internet of Things
Cold chain
Fruit quality prediction
CatBoost classifier
ABSTRACT
Food waste is a significant global problem that demands immediate action to reduce it. This study presents a
novel framework that merges Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) technologies to detect fruit
ripenessandspoilage,whichisessentialinminimizinglossesinthecoldchainprocessoffreshproduceindustry.
The study employed temperature, humidity, and gas emission sensors along with an ESP32 microcontroller to
establish a unique framework that achieved exceptional accuracy in predicting banana ripeness stages. This
framework employedvarious machinelearning algorithmstodetect ripenessstages, with theCatBoost classifier
exhibiting exceptional performance, demonstrating its dependability and effectiveness in assessing fruit quality.
Thebenefitsofthisresearchextendbeyondfruitripenessdetectionandpavethewayforfutureadvancementsin
automating quality assessment in agricultural supply chains.
1. Introduction
Food waste is a pressing problem globally and in India, which pre-
sentssignificantenvironmentalandsocioeconomicchallenges.InIndia,
withitsgrowingurbanizationandpopulation,approximately1.3billion
tonnes of food is wasted annually. That amounts to the produce of
approximately28%ofthecountry’stotalagriculturalland.EachIndian
citizen generates 0.5 kg of organic waste daily. The United Nations Sus-
tainable Development Goal 12.3aimstohalveglobalfoodwasteby2030,
acknowledging its detrimental impact on land, water, energy, and
greenhouse gas emissions [1,2]. An estimated 40–50 % of the world’s
fruits and vegetables are lost or wasted throughout the supply chain,
accounting for approximately half of all food waste [2]. This leads to a
waste of resources, unnecessary greenhouse gas emissions, and sub-
stantialeconomicloss[3].Therefore,reducingfoodwasteinthesupply
chainisessentialforbothenvironmentalandeconomicreasons.Various
factors contribute to high losses in the fresh fruit and vegetable sector,
including weather and the lack of alternative markets. Ludwig-Ohm
et al., [4] investigated on strawberries, apples, lettuce, and carrots and
found out that, on average, 25 % of vegetables, 15 % to 20 % of
strawberriesand6%to16%ofapplesarelostatthefarmlevel.Mostof
the food waste is attributed to fruits, vegetables, and grains. But to
reduce losses, precautionary measures like protected cultivation,
continuous cooling, improved packaging, and staff training need to be
considered. Besides that, increased cooperation between growers,
wholesalers, and retailers can enhance the marketable product share.
This highlights the importance of the environment in maintaining
freshnessandsafety.Itiscrucialtocontinuouslymonitortheircondition
toensuretheirqualityandnutritionalvalue.Astheconventionalmeans
of tracking the condition of produce in supply chains is outdated and
lackdigitalization,therapidspoilageoftheseitemsnecessitatescareful
storage and transportation to extend their shelf life and preserve their
post-harvestquality[5].Theripenessoffruitsisafundamentalaspectof
agricultural production and supply chain industry. It is a critical deter-
minant of the quality and market value of fruits, impacting both pro-
ducers and consumers. For farmers and producers, accurate and timely
ripeness detection is essential for optimizing harvesting schedules,
reducingpost-harvestlosses,andensuringthatfruitsreachconsumersin
their prime condition. Consumers, on the other hand, rely on the ripe-
ness of fruits to make informed purchasing decisions, seeking produce
thatmeetstheirtastepreferencesandnutritionalrequirements[6].Fruit
ripeness assessment typically relies on visual inspection by skilled
personnel; however, this method is subjective, time-consuming, and
prone to errors due to external factors such as fatigue and bias.
Present study considered banana fruit as India is one of the largest
producers of Banana. Its availability throughout the year made it

cold chain processes, there is large amount of spoilage in banana pro-
duce resulting losses to the farmers as well as producers [7–10]. The
losses are mainly due to lapses in assessing banana ripeness. The con-
ventionalmethodofobservingmanuallyisnotadvisable,becauseeven
if the professionals involved, inconsistencies arise from individual var-
iations in perception. Therefore, the authors of this article proposed an
automated system for analysing banana ripeness using emerging tech-
nologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine learning
algorithms.
TheprimaryaimofthisstudyistopresentanIoTsystemintegrated
with a machine-learning technique for fruit ripeness detection and
spoilage reduction in banana.
The following are the key contributions of this work:
1. This study addresses the pressing global issue of food security and
contributestothereductionoffruitwastebyproposingamethodto
detect fruit freshness or spoilage before it occurs.
2. A novelframeworkwasdevelopedthatharnessesthecapabilitiesof
IoT sensors and machine learning techniques to effectively evaluate
and monitor banana ripeness, offering a practical solution to the
identified problem.
3. The successful integration of two key sensors, namely SHT40 and
SGP30, alongside an ESP32 Development board, is demonstrated as
the core component of the proposed system. These sensors play a
crucial role in capturing emissions from fruits and facilitating the
assessment of their ripeness and overall quality.
4. Through extensive experimentation employing various machine
learningalgorithms,theresearchachievedahighlevelofaccuracyin
classifying sensor data over a one-week period. Notably, the Cat-
Boost classifier stands out for its exceptional accuracy in evaluating
the collected data.
2. Literaturereview
The Internet of Things (IoT) is a system that integrates physical ob-
jects and communication technologies to create a networked world
where devices can communicate with each other. Technologies such as
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, radio-frequency identification (RFID), and Wireless
Sensor Networks (WSNs) enable interconnectivity. IoT goes beyond
traditional web browsing and allows remote monitoring and control of
physical environments [11]. The integration of modern technologies,
such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML), offers
thepotentialtorevolutionizetheassessmentoffruitripeness.TheIoT’s
ability to collect real-time data and ML’s capacity to analyse complex
datasets make it possible to develop automated, data-driven solutions
forfruitripenessdetection.Despitenumerousstudiesutilizingadvanced
technologiesforripenessdetection,thereislimitedresearchexamining
the efficacy of these technologies in evaluating fruit ripeness and
spoilage.
The emergence of IoT, Machine learning, and Artificial Neural Net-
works(ANN)impactedthemonitoringandtrackingofcoldchainsystem

This investigation will focus primarily on bananas, as they are widely
consumed in India. Besides that, they have numerous potential appli-
cationsforresearch,particularlyindetectingripenessandspoilage.The
rapid ripening process of bananas makes them an ideal subject for
studying ripeness indicators. Analysis of gases emitted during various
ripeningstagescanprovidevaluableinformationthatcanbecorrelated
withmachinelearningalgorithms.Thisstudyaimedtodevelopmachine
learning-based methods for fruit ripeness and spoilage detection, to
enhancefoodqualitymanagementandsupplychainlogisticsinpractical

3. Methodology
Fig. 1. shows the schematic layout of the proposed experimental
arrangementwithallthenecessarycomponents.TheyincludeIoT-based
sensornodedesign,cloud,datasetdevelopment,andmachinelearning.
3.1. Sensor node design
The sensor node is the combination of the microcontroller and the
sensors.ItconsistsofanESP32microcontroller,SHT40temperatureand
humidity sensor, and SGP30 gas sensor. These components are con-
nected as shown in the schematic diagram in Fig. 2. As ESP32 can
provideWi-Ficonnectivity,andpowerfulprocessing,thesensornodeis
readyforconnectivityandprocessingcomplexdataalso.ESP32operates
as the central processing unit of the sensor node, functioning as a mi-
crocontroller with built-in Wi-Fi capabilities that enable wireless
communication and data transmission. The SHT40 Temperature & Hu-
midity Sensor is incorporated into the Sensor node and measures tem-
peratureandhumiditypreciselywiththehelpofcapacitivesensing.The
SHT40sensorisinterfacedwiththeESP32microcontrollerusinganI2C
communicationprotocol.TheI2Ccommunicationprotocolisemployed
toretrievehumidityandtemperaturedatafromthesensorandconvertit
into relative humidity and temperature readings using appropriate
mathematical formulas.
The SGP30 Indoor Air Quality Sensor developed by Sensirion, was
specifically designed for precise gas sensing in indoor environments.
This compact, energy-efficient sensor incorporates multi-pixel gas
sensor technology, enabling accurate measurements of Total Volatile
Organic Compounds (TVOC) and Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2eq)
levels, as well as H2 and Ethanol levels, which are essential for evalu-
atingindoorairquality.TheSGP30sensor’sI2Cinterfaceandadvanced
signalprocessingalgorithmsdelivercomprehensiveinsightsintoindoor
air quality, empowering users to create healthier living environments
through appropriateactions. The SGP30gas sensor operates withinthe
recommended temperature and humidity ranges, ensuring optimal
performance and longevity. Connecting the SGP30 gas sensor with the
ESP32 microcontroller via I2C protocol enabled gas detection and air
quality monitoring. Sensor node firmware on the ESP32 is developed
and deployed with the help of Arduino IDE.
In the investigation, a plastic container was employed to store ba-
nanas, and a sensor node was attached to measure the gases emitted
during the ripening process, as shown in Fig. 3. Time-series data were
gatheredfromtherawbananastothepointofspoilageusingthissensor
node.

The ThingSpeak platform, which is known for its dependability,
playsacrucialroleinthedesignofsensornodes.UtilizingThingSpeak’s
real-time data visualization platform provides immediate insights into
the fruit ripening conditions. ThingSpeak comprises channels, each of
whichoffersstoragespacefordata.Theinitialstepinvolvesthecreation
of a ThingSpeak channel that serves as a virtual platform for gathering
and processing sensors or device-generated data. During the setup
phase,itisnecessarytocreateanaccountontheThingSpeakCloudand
configure essential parameters, such as privacy settings and metadata.
Additionally, unique API keys must be obtained to facilitate seamless
communicationbetweenthesensornodeandtheplatform.ThingSpeak
offers various applications such as ThingTweet, ThingHTTP, and React
to facilitate integration. Custom applications can also be developed
using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to tailor the solutions to specific IoT
project requirements. Overall, this study considers ThingSpeak as a
versatile platform for IoT development with a range of features and
tools. ThingSpeak significantly enriched this research by providing a
robustinfrastructurefordatamanagementandanalysis,contributingto
the success and scientific significance of this research.

The dataset can be accessed in the form of a CSV file from the

3.3. Data processing
This research incorporated rigorous data cleaning and feature engi-
neeringprocedurestoensurethereliabilityandaccuracyofthegathered
data.Duringthisphase,thedatafromthesensorsandtheirrelationship
with the ripening process of bananas will be observed. These findings
are essential for further exploration and analysis of experimental out-
comes,ultimatelycontributingtoadeeperunderstandingofthebanana
ripening process and the utility of sensor-based monitoring systems in
agricultural contexts. Data pre-processing was performed using Python
libraries such as NumPy and Pandas, focusing on several key tasks:
1. Outlier Detection and Handling: Outliers were identified and
managed using the Interquartile Range (IQR) technique. This
approach involved calculating the IQR and applying it to filter out
anomalous data points that could skew the analysis.
2. Date Formatting: Dates were standardized to ensure consistency
across the dataset, facilitating accurate time-series analysis and
comparisons.
3. Null Value Management: We systematically checked for and
removednullvaluesfromthedatasettoavoidanypotentialbiasesor
inaccuracies in subsequent analyses.
Thesedata-cleaningstepswerecrucialintransformingrawdatainto
a well-structured format suitable for machine learning. By addressing
outliers, ensuring consistent date formatting, and eliminating null
values, we prepared the data for reliable and insightful analysis.
The dataset was carefully labelled with appropriate designations of
fruitripeness,encompassingthecategoriesofnotripe,ripe,andspoiled.
In the Data Analysis phase, we meticulously examined key variables,
includingtemperature,humidity,H2,Ethanol,CO2,andTVOC.Thedata
was categorized into three ripeness stages—Not ripe, Ripe, and Spoil-
ed—basedonthecombinationofvisualinspectionofcameraimagesand
TVOCvalues.Fig.5depictsthevaryingdegreesofripenessforbananas,
including those that are not ripe, ripe, or spoiled. Data for each stage

The criteria for these categories were as follows:
• Not Ripe: Characterized by a green to pale green colour, firm
texture, and a thick, inflexible peel.
• Ripe:Markedbyabrightyellowcolour(withpossiblegreentips),a
softer yet still firm texture, and a thinner, more flexible peel. The
presence of some brown spots may be observed.
• Spoiled:Identifiedbyayellowcolourwithextensivebrownspotsor
a completely brown peel, a very soft and mushy texture, and sig-
nificant changes in TVOC values.
These classifications enabled a structured analysis of the ripening
process and supported the development of predictive models.
Thesecriteriawereconsistentlyappliedtobothtrainingandtestsets
for accurate classification. Following data cleaning, extensive data
analysis was performed using appropriate statistical methods and
techniques. The Key observationsof this analysis can be observed from
Fig. 7, and they include:
• TVOC: Increased in ripe and spoiled stages.
• Ethanol: Decreased in the spoiled stage.
• H2: Decreased overall.
• CO2: Increased in ripe and spoiled stages.
These findings are crucial for further exploration of experimental
outcomes and contribute to a deeper understanding of the banana
ripening process. They also highlight the utility of sensor-based moni-
toring systems in agricultural contexts. By examining these trends, a
machine-learningmodelcanbedevelopedtopredictfruitqualityusing
this dataset.
3.4. Machine learning for fruit quality prediction
Thecategorizationoffruitsintovaryingstagesofripeness,including
not ripe, ripe, and spoiled, was based on input features derived from the
sensor data. The functionality of the machine learning model was
assessed using pertinent evaluation metrics such as a classification
report, confusion matrix, and accuracy scores. These metrics provide a
comprehensive understanding of the model’s predictive capabilities,
precision in different ripeness categories, and overall accuracy in fruit
ripeness prediction. The machine-learning approach demonstrated the
potential for automationinfruit ripenessdetection andhighlightedthe
significanceofemployinginterpretablemodelsinagriculturalandfood
supply chain applications, where transparency and explainability are
crucial.
The research involved a rigorous machine-learning evaluation pro-
cess to enable the device to predict banana ripeness stages based on
sensordata.Thedatasetwasdividedintotrainingandtestsets.Various
algorithms,includingtheRandomForestClassifier(RFC),DecisionTree
Classifier (DTC), Support Vector Machines (SVM), AdaBoost Classifier
(ADB), andCatBoost Classifier (CBC),were used to trainthemodels on
thetrainingset.Thetrainedmodelswerethenusedtomakepredictions
on the test set. After generating predictions, the performance of each
model was evaluated by comparing the predicted ripeness stages with
the actual labels from the test set. This evaluation provided valuable
insights into the effectiveness and performance characteristics of each
model, enabling informed decisions regarding their deployment in
practical applications. To ensure a comprehensive evaluation of the
machine learning models utilized in this study, detailed parameter set-
tings and training procedures for each algorithm are essential. The
configuration parameters for the ML algorithms considered are given
below.
• Random Forest Classifier (RFC): The model was configured with 100
estimators and a random state of 42 to ensure reproducibility. The
RFC was trained on the normalized training dataset, and its perfor-
mance was assessed using accuracy metrics on the test set.
• Decision Tree Classifier (DTC):Itwassetwitharandomstateof21to
facilitateconsistentresults.Thetraininginvolvedfittingthemodelto
the normalized data, with performance evaluated based on test set
predictions compared to actual labels.
• K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm:Themodelwasconfiguredwith
5 neighbours, a choice that balances sensitivity and specificity. The
KNN model was trained on the normalized dataset, and its effec-
tiveness was measured through predictions on the test set.
• Support Vector Machine (SVM): The model was configured with a
random state of 21 to maintain consistency. The training involved
fitting the model to the normalized training data, and performance
was gauged based on its predictions on the test set.
• CatBoost Classifier (CBC): It underwent a rigorous hyperparameter
optimization process using Optuna. Initial settings included a
random seed of 21. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, depth,
colsample_bylevel, min_data_in_leaf, and bootstrap_type were opti-
mized.Thelearningraterangedfrom1e-3to0.1,depthfrom1to10,
colsample_bylevel from 0.05 to 1.0, and min_data_in_leaf from 1 to
100, with bootstrap_type selected from ’Bernoulli’ and ’MVS’. The
subsample parameter was optimized when bootstrap_type was not
’Bayesian’. The model was trained with the best-found hyper-
parameters, and accuracy was evaluated on the test set.AdaBoost
Classifier (ABC):Itwasconfiguredwith50boostingiterationsanda
learning rate of 0.005. The model was trained on the normalized
trainingdata,anditsperformancewasevaluatedthroughpredictions
on the test set.

4. Resultsanddiscussion
Data analysis was performed using the appropriate statistical
methods andtechniques. Upon analysing the primarycharacteristics of
the dataset, several noteworthy relationships were discovered. Before
that, it is better to review the physiological relationship between pa-
rametersconsideredindeterminingbananaripeness.Thephysiological
relationship between the parameters measured—such as temperature,
humidity, TVOC, ethanol, and other volatile compounds—and the ba-
nanaripeningprocessiscrucialforunderstandingthedataobtainedand
its relevance.
• Temperature: As bananas ripen, their metabolic rate increases,
leadingtohigherrespirationandethyleneproduction,whichinturn
affects the temperature of the fruit. Studies have shown that tem-
perature significantly impacts the ripening speed and quality of ba-
nanas. For instance, elevated temperatures can accelerate ripening,
leading to faster colour change and texture softening.
• Humidity: Humidity levels influence the rate of moisture loss from
bananas, affecting their texture and shelf life. High humidity can
slowdowntheripeningprocessbyreducingtherateofmoistureloss,
whilelowhumiditycanleadtoprematuredehydrationandspoilage
[34].

spoilage detection: A case study on bananas
Rajini Ma,*, Persis Voolab
a Department of CSE, Government Degree College, Ravulapalem, A.P, India

ABSTRACT
Food waste is a significant global problem that demands immediate action to reduce it. This study presents a
novel framework that merges Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) technologies to detect fruit
ripenessandspoilage,whichisessentialinminimizinglossesinthecoldchainprocessoffreshproduceindustry.
The study employed temperature, humidity, and gas emission sensors along with an ESP32 microcontroller to
establish a unique framework that achieved exceptional accuracy in predicting banana ripeness stages. This
framework employedvarious machinelearning algorithmstodetect ripenessstages, with theCatBoost classifier
exhibiting exceptional performance, demonstrating its dependability and effectiveness in assessing fruit quality.
Thebenefitsofthisresearchextendbeyondfruitripenessdetectionandpavethewayforfutureadvancementsin
automating quality assessment in agricultural supply chains.
1. Introduction
Food waste is a pressing problem globally and in India, which pre-
sentssignificantenvironmentalandsocioeconomicchallenges.InIndia,
withitsgrowingurbanizationandpopulation,approximately1.3billion
tonnes of food is wasted annually. That amounts to the produce of
approximately28%ofthecountry’stotalagriculturalland.EachIndian
citizen generates 0.5 kg of organic waste daily. The United Nations Sus-
tainable Development Goal 12.3aimstohalveglobalfoodwasteby2030,
acknowledging its detrimental impact on land, water, energy, and
greenhouse gas emissions [1,2]. An estimated 40–50 % of the world’s
fruits and vegetables are lost or wasted throughout the supply chain,
accounting for approximately half of all food waste [2]. This leads to a
waste of resources, unnecessary greenhouse gas emissions, and sub-
stantialeconomicloss[3].Therefore,reducingfoodwasteinthesupply
chainisessentialforbothenvironmentalandeconomicreasons.Various
factors contribute to high losses in the fresh fruit and vegetable sector,
including weather and the lack of alternative markets. Ludwig-Ohm
et al., [4] investigated on strawberries, apples, lettuce, and carrots and
found out that, on average, 25 % of vegetables, 15 % to 20 % of
strawberriesand6%to16%ofapplesarelostatthefarmlevel.Mostof
the food waste is attributed to fruits, vegetables, and grains. But to
reduce losses, precautionary measures like protected cultivation,
continuous cooling, improved packaging, and staff training need to be
considered. Besides that, increased cooperation between growers,
wholesalers, and retailers can enhance the marketable product share.
This highlights the importance of the environment in maintaining
freshnessandsafety.Itiscrucialtocontinuouslymonitortheircondition
toensuretheirqualityandnutritionalvalue.Astheconventionalmeans
of tracking the condition of produce in supply chains is outdated and
lackdigitalization,therapidspoilageoftheseitemsnecessitatescareful
storage and transportation to extend their shelf life and preserve their
post-harvestquality[5].Theripenessoffruitsisafundamentalaspectof
agricultural production and supply chain industry. It is a critical deter-
minant of the quality and market value of fruits, impacting both pro-
ducers and consumers. For farmers and producers, accurate and timely
ripeness detection is essential for optimizing harvesting schedules,
reducingpost-harvestlosses,andensuringthatfruitsreachconsumersin
their prime condition. Consumers, on the other hand, rely on the ripe-
ness of fruits to make informed purchasing decisions, seeking produce
thatmeetstheirtastepreferencesandnutritionalrequirements[6].Fruit
ripeness assessment typically relies on visual inspection by skilled
personnel; however, this method is subjective, time-consuming, and
prone to errors due to external factors such as fatigue and bias.
Present study considered banana fruit as India is one of the largest
producers of Banana. Its availability throughout the year made it

people’s choice. However, due to infrastructural issues in logistics and
cold chain processes, there is large amount of spoilage in banana pro-
duce resulting losses to the farmers as well as producers [7–10]. The
losses are mainly due to lapses in assessing banana ripeness. The con-
ventionalmethodofobservingmanuallyisnotadvisable,becauseeven
if the professionals involved, inconsistencies arise from individual var-
iations in perception. Therefore, the authors of this article proposed an
automated system for analysing banana ripeness using emerging tech-
nologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine learning
algorithms.
TheprimaryaimofthisstudyistopresentanIoTsystemintegrated
with a machine-learning technique for fruit ripeness detection and
spoilage reduction in banana.
The following are the key contributions of this work:
1. This study addresses the pressing global issue of food security and
contributestothereductionoffruitwastebyproposingamethodto
detect fruit freshness or spoilage before it occurs.
2. A novelframeworkwasdevelopedthatharnessesthecapabilitiesof
IoT sensors and machine learning techniques to effectively evaluate
and monitor banana ripeness, offering a practical solution to the
identified problem.
3. The successful integration of two key sensors, namely SHT40 and
SGP30, alongside an ESP32 Development board, is demonstrated as
the core component of the proposed system. These sensors play a
crucial role in capturing emissions from fruits and facilitating the
assessment of their ripeness and overall quality.
4. Through extensive experimentation employing various machine
learningalgorithms,theresearchachievedahighlevelofaccuracyin
classifying sensor data over a one-week period. Notably, the Cat-
Boost classifier stands out for its exceptional accuracy in evaluating
the collected data.
2. Literaturereview
The Internet of Things (IoT) is a system that integrates physical ob-
jects and communication technologies to create a networked world
where devices can communicate with each other. Technologies such as

3.1. Sensor node design
The sensor node is the combination of the microcontroller and the
sensors.ItconsistsofanESP32microcontroller,SHT40temperatureand
humidity sensor, and SGP30 gas sensor. These components are con-
nected as shown in the schematic diagram in Fig. 2. As ESP32 can
provideWi-Ficonnectivity,andpowerfulprocessing,thesensornodeis
readyforconnectivityandprocessingcomplexdataalso.ESP32operates
as the central processing unit of the sensor node, functioning as a mi-
crocontroller with built-in Wi-Fi capabilities that enable wireless
communication and data transmission. The SHT40 Temperature & Hu-
midity Sensor is incorporated into the Sensor node and measures tem-
peratureandhumiditypreciselywiththehelpofcapacitivesensing.The
SHT40sensorisinterfacedwiththeESP32microcontrollerusinganI2C
communicationprotocol.TheI2Ccommunicationprotocolisemployed
toretrievehumidityandtemperaturedatafromthesensorandconvertit
into relative humidity and temperature readings using appropriate
mathematical formulas.
The SGP30 Indoor Air Quality Sensor developed by Sensirion, was
specifically designed for precise gas sensing in indoor environments.
This compact, energy-efficient sensor incorporates multi-pixel gas
sensor technology, enabling accurate measurements of Total Volatile
Organic Compounds (TVOC) and Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2eq)
levels, as well as H2 and Ethanol levels, which are essential for evalu-
atingindoorairquality.TheSGP30sensor’sI2Cinterfaceandadvanced
signalprocessingalgorithmsdelivercomprehensiveinsightsintoindoor
air quality, empowering users to create healthier living environments
through appropriateactions. The SGP30gas sensor operates withinthe
recommended temperature and humidity ranges, ensuring optimal
performance and longevity. Connecting the SGP30 gas sensor with the
ESP32 microcontroller via I2C protocol enabled gas detection and air
quality monitoring. Sensor node firmware on the ESP32 is developed
and deployed with the help of Arduino IDE.

5. Conclusion
In conclusion, the results of our study demonstrate the promising
potential of integrating Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning
(ML) technologies in automating fruit ripeness assessment. Our pro-
posed framework, which employed various ML algorithms, found that
the CatBoost Classifier achieves high accuracy in predicting banana
ripenessstages.Thisishighwhencomparedtootherstudiesfocusedon
fruit ripeness. This superiority highlighted the dependability and effi-
ciency of our model for advancing the field of fruit quality assessment.
The scope of future research in this area is vast, with opportunities for
explorationandimprovement.Thepotentialoftheframeworktoassess
ripeness stages invarious fruits beyond bananas isworth investigating.
Moreover, optimizing the algorithm and dataset can lead to increased
accuracy and more versatile applications for fruit ripeness evaluation.

DevelopinganIoTandML-drivenplatformforfruitripenessevaluationand
spoilage detection: A case study on bananas
Rajini Ma,*, Persis Voolab
a Department of CSE, Government Degree College, Ravulapalem, A.P, India
b Department of CSE, Adikavi Nannaya University, Rajahmundry, A.P, India
ARTICLE INFO
Keywords:
Internet of Things
Cold chain
Fruit quality prediction
CatBoost classifier
ABSTRACT
Food waste is a significant global problem that demands immediate action to reduce it. This study presents a
novel framework that merges Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) technologies to detect fruit
ripenessandspoilage,whichisessentialinminimizinglossesinthecoldchainprocessoffreshproduceindustry.
The study employed temperature, humidity, and gas emission sensors along with an ESP32 microcontroller to
establish a unique framework that achieved exceptional accuracy in predicting banana ripeness stages. This
framework employedvarious machinelearning algorithmstodetect ripenessstages, with theCatBoost classifier
exhibiting exceptional performance, demonstrating its dependability and effectiveness in assessing fruit quality.
Thebenefitsofthisresearchextendbeyondfruitripenessdetectionandpavethewayforfutureadvancementsin
automating quality assessment in agricultural supply chains.
1. Introduction
Food waste is a pressing problem globally and in India, which pre-
sentssignificantenvironmentalandsocioeconomicchallenges.InIndia,
withitsgrowingurbanizationandpopulation,approximately1.3billion
tonnes of food is wasted annually. That amounts to the produce of
approximately28%ofthecountry’stotalagriculturalland.EachIndian
citizen generates 0.5 kg of organic waste daily. The United Nations Sus-
tainable Development Goal 12.3aimstohalveglobalfoodwasteby2030,
acknowledging its detrimental impact on land, water, energy, and
greenhouse gas emissions [1,2]. An estimated 40–50 % of the world’s
fruits and vegetables are lost or wasted throughout the supply chain,
accounting for approximately half of all food waste [2]. This leads to a
waste of resources, unnecessary greenhouse gas emissions, and sub-
stantialeconomicloss[3].Therefore,reducingfoodwasteinthesupply
chainisessentialforbothenvironmentalandeconomicreasons.Various
factors contribute to high losses in the fresh fruit and vegetable sector,
including weather and the lack of alternative markets. Ludwig-Ohm
et al., [4] investigated on strawberries, apples, lettuce, and carrots and
found out that, on average, 25 % of vegetables, 15 % to 20 % of
strawberriesand6%to16%ofapplesarelostatthefarmlevel.Mostof
the food waste is attributed to fruits, vegetables, and grains. But to
reduce losses, precautionary measures like protected cultivation,
continuous cooling, improved packaging, and staff training need to be
considered. Besides that, increased cooperation between growers,
wholesalers, and retailers can enhance the marketable product share.
This highlights the importance of the environment in maintaining
freshnessandsafety.Itiscrucialtocontinuouslymonitortheircondition
toensuretheirqualityandnutritionalvalue.Astheconventionalmeans
of tracking the condition of produce in supply chains is outdated and
lackdigitalization,therapidspoilageoftheseitemsnecessitatescareful
storage and transportation to extend their shelf life and preserve their
post-harvestquality[5].Theripenessoffruitsisafundamentalaspectof
agricultural production and supply chain industry. It is a critical deter-
minant of the quality and market value of fruits, impacting both pro-
ducers and consumers. For farmers and producers, accurate and timely
ripeness detection is essential for optimizing harvesting schedules,
reducingpost-harvestlosses,andensuringthatfruitsreachconsumersin
their prime condition. Consumers, on the other hand, rely on the ripe-
ness of fruits to make informed purchasing decisions, seeking produce
thatmeetstheirtastepreferencesandnutritionalrequirements[6].Fruit
ripeness assessment typically relies on visual inspection by skilled
personnel; however, this method is subjective, time-consuming, and
prone to errors due to external factors such as fatigue and bias.
Present study considered banana fruit as India is one of the largest
producers of Banana. Its availability throughout the year made it

cold chain processes, there is large amount of spoilage in banana pro-
duce resulting losses to the farmers as well as producers [7–10]. The
losses are mainly due to lapses in assessing banana ripeness. The con-
ventionalmethodofobservingmanuallyisnotadvisable,becauseeven
if the professionals involved, inconsistencies arise from individual var-
iations in perception. Therefore, the authors of this article proposed an
automated system for analysing banana ripeness using emerging tech-
nologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine learning
algorithms.
TheprimaryaimofthisstudyistopresentanIoTsystemintegrated
with a machine-learning technique for fruit ripeness detection and
spoilage reduction in banana.
The following are the key contributions of this work:
1. This study addresses the pressing global issue of food security and
contributestothereductionoffruitwastebyproposingamethodto
detect fruit freshness or spoilage before it occurs.
2. A novelframeworkwasdevelopedthatharnessesthecapabilitiesof
IoT sensors and machine learning techniques to effectively evaluate
and monitor banana ripeness, offering a practical solution to the
identified problem.
3. The successful integration of two key sensors, namely SHT40 and
SGP30, alongside an ESP32 Development board, is demonstrated as
the core component of the proposed system. These sensors play a
crucial role in capturing emissions from fruits and facilitating the
assessment of their ripeness and overall quality.
4. Through extensive experimentation employing various machine
learningalgorithms,theresearchachievedahighlevelofaccuracyin
classifying sensor data over a one-week period. Notably, the Cat-
Boost classifier stands out for its exceptional accuracy in evaluating
the collected data.
2. Literaturereview
The Internet of Things (IoT) is a system that integrates physical ob-
jects and communication technologies to create a networked world
where devices can communicate with each other. Technologies such as
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, radio-frequency identification (RFID), and Wireless
Sensor Networks (WSNs) enable interconnectivity. IoT goes beyond
traditional web browsing and allows remote monitoring and control of
physical environments [11]. The integration of modern technologies,
such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML), offers
thepotentialtorevolutionizetheassessmentoffruitripeness.TheIoT’s
ability to collect real-time data and ML’s capacity to analyse complex
datasets make it possible to develop automated, data-driven solutions
forfruitripenessdetection.Despitenumerousstudiesutilizingadvanced
technologiesforripenessdetection,thereislimitedresearchexamining
the efficacy of these technologies in evaluating fruit ripeness and
spoilage.
The emergence of IoT, Machine learning, and Artificial Neural Net-
works(ANN)impactedthemonitoringandtrackingofcoldchainsystem
inaradicalway.Severalstudiesfocussedonharnessingtheadvantages

• The methods used by researchers to assess/monitor the quality of

The proposed framework evaluates the performance of state-of-the-
art sensors for measuring the gases emitted by fruits, temperature, and
humidity. Subsequently, advanced machine-learning algorithms were
applied to predict the ripeness of the fruit based on the collected data.
This investigation will focus primarily on bananas, as they are widely
consumed in India. Besides that, they have numerous potential appli-
cationsforresearch,particularlyindetectingripenessandspoilage.The
rapid ripening process of bananas makes them an ideal subject for
studying ripeness indicators. Analysis of gases emitted during various
ripeningstagescanprovidevaluableinformationthatcanbecorrelated
withmachinelearningalgorithms.Thisstudyaimedtodevelopmachine
learning-based methods for fruit ripeness and spoilage detection, to
enhancefoodqualitymanagementandsupplychainlogisticsinpractical
settings.Theproposedframeworkdemonstratesremarkableaccuracyin
monitoring the quality of fruits and vegetables in retail store trays or
cold storagesupplychains,presentingapractical andfeasiblesolution.
3. Methodology
Fig. 1. shows the schematic layout of the proposed experimental
arrangementwithallthenecessarycomponents.TheyincludeIoT-based
sensornodedesign,cloud,datasetdevelopment,andmachinelearning.
3.1. Sensor node design
The sensor node is the combination of the microcontroller and the
sensors.ItconsistsofanESP32microcontroller,SHT40temperatureand
humidity sensor, and SGP30 gas sensor. These components are con-
nected as shown in the schematic diagram in Fig. 2. As ESP32 can
provideWi-Ficonnectivity,andpowerfulprocessing,thesensornodeis
readyforconnectivityandprocessingcomplexdataalso.ESP32operates
as the central processing unit of the sensor node, functioning as a mi-
crocontroller with built-in Wi-Fi capabilities that enable wireless
communication and data transmission. The SHT40 Temperature & Hu-
midity Sensor is incorporated into the Sensor node and measures tem-
peratureandhumiditypreciselywiththehelpofcapacitivesensing.The
SHT40sensorisinterfacedwiththeESP32microcontrollerusinganI2C
communicationprotocol.TheI2Ccommunicationprotocolisemployed
toretrievehumidityandtemperaturedatafromthesensorandconvertit
into relative humidity and temperature readings using appropriate
mathematical formulas.
The SGP30 Indoor Air Quality Sensor developed by Sensirion, was
specifically designed for precise gas sensing in indoor environments.
This compact, energy-efficient sensor incorporates multi-pixel gas
sensor technology, enabling accurate measurements of Total Volatile
Organic Compounds (TVOC) and Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2eq)
levels, as well as H2 and Ethanol levels, which are essential for evalu-
atingindoorairquality.TheSGP30sensor’sI2Cinterfaceandadvanced
signalprocessingalgorithmsdelivercomprehensiveinsightsintoindoor
air quality, empowering users to create healthier living environments
through appropriateactions. The SGP30gas sensor operates withinthe
recommended temperature and humidity ranges, ensuring optimal
performance and longevity. Connecting the SGP30 gas sensor with the
ESP32 microcontroller via I2C protocol enabled gas detection and air
quality monitoring. Sensor node firmware on the ESP32 is developed
and deployed with the help of Arduino IDE.
In the investigation, a plastic container was employed to store ba-
nanas, and a sensor node was attached to measure the gases emitted
during the ripening process, as shown in Fig. 3. Time-series data were
gatheredfromtherawbananastothepointofspoilageusingthissensor
node.
3.2. ThingSpeak cloud and data collection
The ThingSpeak platform, which is known for its dependability,
playsacrucialroleinthedesignofsensornodes.UtilizingThingSpeak’s
real-time data visualization platform provides immediate insights into
the fruit ripening conditions. ThingSpeak comprises channels, each of
whichoffersstoragespacefordata.Theinitialstepinvolvesthecreation

potential of integrating Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning
(ML) technologies in automating fruit ripeness assessment. Our pro-

the CatBoost Classifier achieves high accuracy in predicting banana
ripenessstages.Thisishighwhencomparedtootherstudiesfocusedon
fruit ripeness. This superiority highlighted the dependability and effi-
ciency of our model for advancing the field of fruit quality assessment.
The scope of future research in this area is vast, with opportunities for
explorationandimprovement.Thepotentialoftheframeworktoassess

Moreover, optimizing the algorithm and dataset can lead to increased
accuracy and more versatile applications for fruit ripeness evaluation.

ABSTRACT
Food waste is a significant global problem that demands immediate action to reduce it. This study presents a
novel framework that merges Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) technologies to detect fruit
ripenessandspoilage,whichisessentialinminimizinglossesinthecoldchainprocessoffreshproduceindustry.
The study employed temperature, humidity, and gas emission sensors along with an ESP32 microcontroller to
establish a unique framework that achieved exceptional accuracy in predicting banana ripeness stages. This
framework employedvarious machinelearning algorithmstodetect ripenessstages, with theCatBoost classifier
exhibiting exceptional performance, demonstrating its dependability and effectiveness in assessing fruit quality.
Thebenefitsofthisresearchextendbeyondfruitripenessdetectionandpavethewayforfutureadvancementsin
automating quality assessment in agricultural supply chains.
1. Introduction
Food waste is a pressing problem globally and in India, which pre-
sentssignificantenvironmentalandsocioeconomicchallenges.InIndia,
withitsgrowingurbanizationandpopulation,approximately1.3billion
tonnes of food is wasted annually. That amounts to the produce of
approximately28%ofthecountry’stotalagriculturalland.EachIndian
citizen generates 0.5 kg of organic waste daily. The United Nations Sus-
tainable Development Goal 12.3aimstohalveglobalfoodwasteby2030,
acknowledging its detrimental impact on land, water, energy, and
greenhouse gas emissions [1,2]. An estimated 40–50 % of the world’s
fruits and vegetables are lost or wasted throughout the supply chain,
accounting for approximately half of all food waste [2]. This leads to a
waste of resources, unnecessary greenhouse gas emissions, and sub-
stantialeconomicloss[3].Therefore,reducingfoodwasteinthesupply
chainisessentialforbothenvironmentalandeconomicreasons.Various
factors contribute to high losses in the fresh fruit and vegetable sector,
including weather and the lack of alternative markets. Ludwig-Ohm
et al., [4] investigated on strawberries, apples, lettuce, and carrots and
found out that, on average, 25 % of vegetables, 15 % to 20 % of
strawberriesand6%to16%ofapplesarelostatthefarmlevel.Mostof
the food waste is attributed to fruits, vegetables, and grains. But to
reduce losses, precautionary measures like protected cultivation,
continuous cooling, improved packaging, and staff training need to be
considered. Besides that, increased cooperation between growers,
wholesalers, and retailers can enhance the marketable product share.
This highlights the importance of the environment in maintaining
freshnessandsafety.Itiscrucialtocontinuouslymonitortheircondition
toensuretheirqualityandnutritionalvalue.Astheconventionalmeans
of tracking the condition of produce in supply chains is outdated and
lackdigitalization,therapidspoilageoftheseitemsnecessitatescareful
storage and transportation to extend their shelf life and preserve their
post-harvestquality[5].Theripenessoffruitsisafundamentalaspectof
agricultural production and supply chain industry. It is a critical deter-
minant of the quality and market value of fruits, impacting both pro-
ducers and consumers. For farmers and producers, accurate and timely
ripeness detection is essential for optimizing harvesting schedules,
reducingpost-harvestlosses,andensuringthatfruitsreachconsumersin
their prime condition. Consumers, on the other hand, rely on the ripe-
ness of fruits to make informed purchasing decisions, seeking produce
thatmeetstheirtastepreferencesandnutritionalrequirements[6].Fruit
ripeness assessment typically relies on visual inspection by skilled
personnel; however, this method is subjective, time-consuming, and
prone to errors due to external factors such as fatigue and bias.
Present study considered banana fruit as India is one of the largest
producers of Banana. Its availability throughout the year made it

TheprimaryaimofthisstudyistopresentanIoTsystemintegrated

The following are the key contributions of this work:
1. This study addresses the pressing global issue of food security and

2. A novelframeworkwasdevelopedthatharnessesthecapabilitiesof

identified problem.
3. The successful integration of two key sensors, namely SHT40 and
SGP30, alongside an ESP32 Development board, is demonstrated as
the core component of the proposed system. These sensors play a
crucial role in capturing emissions from fruits and facilitating the

4. Through extensive experimentation employing various machine

3. Methodology
Fig. 1. shows the schematic layout of the proposed experimental
arrangementwithallthenecessarycomponents.TheyincludeIoT-based
sensornodedesign,cloud,datasetdevelopment,andmachinelearning.
3.1. Sensor node design
The sensor node is the combination of the microcontroller and the
sensors.ItconsistsofanESP32microcontroller,SHT40temperatureand
humidity sensor, and SGP30 gas sensor. These components are con-
nected as shown in the schematic diagram in Fig. 2. As ESP32 can
provideWi-Ficonnectivity,andpowerfulprocessing,thesensornodeis
readyforconnectivityandprocessingcomplexdataalso.ESP32operates
as the central processing unit of the sensor node, functioning as a mi-
crocontroller with built-in Wi-Fi capabilities that enable wireless
communication and data transmission. The SHT40 Temperature & Hu-
midity Sensor is incorporated into the Sensor node and measures tem-
peratureandhumiditypreciselywiththehelpofcapacitivesensing.The
SHT40sensorisinterfacedwiththeESP32microcontrollerusinganI2C
communicationprotocol.TheI2Ccommunicationprotocolisemployed
toretrievehumidityandtemperaturedatafromthesensorandconvertit
into relative humidity and temperature readings using appropriate
mathematical formulas.
The SGP30 Indoor Air Quality Sensor developed by Sensirion, was
specifically designed for precise gas sensing in indoor environments.
This compact, energy-efficient sensor incorporates multi-pixel gas
sensor technology, enabling accurate measurements of Total Volatile
Organic Compounds (TVOC) and Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2eq)
levels, as well as H2 and Ethanol levels, which are essential for evalu-
atingindoorairquality.TheSGP30sensor’sI2Cinterfaceandadvanced
signalprocessingalgorithmsdelivercomprehensiveinsightsintoindoor
air quality, empowering users to create healthier living environments
through appropriateactions. The SGP30gas sensor operates withinthe
recommended temperature and humidity ranges, ensuring optimal
performance and longevity. Connecting the SGP30 gas sensor with the
ESP32 microcontroller via I2C protocol enabled gas detection and air
quality monitoring. Sensor node firmware on the ESP32 is developed
and deployed with the help of Arduino IDE.
In the investigation, a plastic container was employed to store ba-
nanas, and a sensor node was attached to measure the gases emitted
during the ripening process, as shown in Fig. 3. Time-series data were
gatheredfromtherawbananastothepointofspoilageusingthissensor
node.
3.2. ThingSpeak cloud and data collection
The ThingSpeak platform, which is known for its dependability,
playsacrucialroleinthedesignofsensornodes.UtilizingThingSpeak’s
real-time data visualization platform provides immediate insights into
the fruit ripening conditions. ThingSpeak comprises channels, each of
whichoffersstoragespacefordata.Theinitialstepinvolvesthecreation
of a ThingSpeak channel that serves as a virtual platform for gathering
and processing sensors or device-generated data. During the setup
phase,itisnecessarytocreateanaccountontheThingSpeakCloudand
configure essential parameters, such as privacy settings and metadata.
Additionally, unique API keys must be obtained to facilitate seamless
communicationbetweenthesensornodeandtheplatform.ThingSpeak
offers various applications such as ThingTweet, ThingHTTP, and React
to facilitate integration. Custom applications can also be developed
using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to tailor the solutions to specific IoT
project requirements. Overall, this study considers ThingSpeak as a
versatile platform for IoT development with a range of features and
tools. ThingSpeak significantly enriched this research by providing a
robustinfrastructurefordatamanagementandanalysis,contributingto
the success and scientific significance of this research.

from various sensors locally and transmits them wirelessly to the

including temperature, humidity, TVOC, CO2, H2, and ethanol mea-
surements, from the ESP32 microcontroller to the cloud. A compre-
hensivedatasetwasdevelopedthroughthecollectionofsensordatafor
7 days. There are two methods to create this dataset. The ThingSpeak
RESTAPIinPythoncanbeusedtogathernecessarydata.Thegraphical
representation of the total data collected during the banana ripeness
process is given in Fig. 4.
The dataset can be accessed in the form of a CSV file from the
ThingSpeakcloudplatform,whichprovidesuserswithalldatacollected
fromvarioussensors,includingtemperature,humidity,TVOC,CO2,and
other significant gas measurements. This extensive dataset is available

and professionals upon request. The variation of key parameters like
temperature,humidity,andgenerationofCO2,H2,EthanolandTVOCin

3.3. Data processing
This research incorporated rigorous data cleaning and feature engi-
neeringprocedurestoensurethereliabilityandaccuracyofthegathered
data.Duringthisphase,thedatafromthesensorsandtheirrelationship
with the ripening process of bananas will be observed. These findings
are essential for further exploration and analysis of experimental out-
comes,ultimatelycontributingtoadeeperunderstandingofthebanana
ripening process and the utility of sensor-based monitoring systems in
agricultural contexts. Data pre-processing was performed using Python
libraries such as NumPy and Pandas, focusing on several key tasks:
1. Outlier Detection and Handling: Outliers were identified and
managed using the Interquartile Range (IQR) technique. This
approach involved calculating the IQR and applying it to filter out
anomalous data points that could skew the analysis.
2. Date Formatting: Dates were standardized to ensure consistency
across the dataset, facilitating accurate time-series analysis and
comparisons.
3. Null Value Management: We systematically checked for and
removednullvaluesfromthedatasettoavoidanypotentialbiasesor
inaccuracies in subsequent analyses.
Thesedata-cleaningstepswerecrucialintransformingrawdatainto
a well-structured format suitable for machine learning. By addressing
outliers, ensuring consistent date formatting, and eliminating null
values, we prepared the data for reliable and insightful analysis.
The dataset was carefully labelled with appropriate designations of
fruitripeness,encompassingthecategoriesofnotripe,ripe,andspoiled.
In the Data Analysis phase, we meticulously examined key variables,
includingtemperature,humidity,H2,Ethanol,CO2,andTVOC.Thedata
was categorized into three ripeness stages—Not ripe, Ripe, and Spoil-
ed—basedonthecombinationofvisualinspectionofcameraimagesand
TVOCvalues.Fig.5depictsthevaryingdegreesofripenessforbananas,
including those that are not ripe, ripe, or spoiled. Data for each stage

were collected using an experimental setup.
The criteria for these categories were as follows:
• Not Ripe: Characterized by a green to pale green colour, firm
texture, and a thick, inflexible peel.
• Ripe:Markedbyabrightyellowcolour(withpossiblegreentips),a
softer yet still firm texture, and a thinner, more flexible peel. The
presence of some brown spots may be observed.
• Spoiled:Identifiedbyayellowcolourwithextensivebrownspotsor
a completely brown peel, a very soft and mushy texture, and sig-
nificant changes in TVOC values.
These classifications enabled a structured analysis of the ripening
process and supported the development of predictive models.
Thesecriteriawereconsistentlyappliedtobothtrainingandtestsets
for accurate classification. Following data cleaning, extensive data
analysis was performed using appropriate statistical methods and
techniques. The Key observationsof this analysis can be observed from
Fig. 7, and they include:
• TVOC: Increased in ripe and spoiled stages.
• Ethanol: Decreased in the spoiled stage.
• H2: Decreased overall.
• CO2: Increased in ripe and spoiled stages.
These findings are crucial for further exploration of experimental
outcomes and contribute to a deeper understanding of the banana
ripening process. They also highlight the utility of sensor-based moni-
toring systems in agricultural contexts. By examining these trends, a
machine-learningmodelcanbedevelopedtopredictfruitqualityusing
this dataset.
3.4. Machine learning for fruit quality prediction
Thecategorizationoffruitsintovaryingstagesofripeness,including
not ripe, ripe, and spoiled, was based on input features derived from the
sensor data. The functionality of the machine learning model was
assessed using pertinent evaluation metrics such as a classification
report, confusion matrix, and accuracy scores. These metrics provide a
comprehensive understanding of the model’s predictive capabilities,
precision in different ripeness categories, and overall accuracy in fruit
ripeness prediction. The machine-learning approach demonstrated the
potential for automationinfruit ripenessdetection andhighlightedthe
significanceofemployinginterpretablemodelsinagriculturalandfood
supply chain applications, where transparency and explainability are
crucial.
The research involved a rigorous machine-learning evaluation pro-
cess to enable the device to predict banana ripeness stages based on
sensordata.Thedatasetwasdividedintotrainingandtestsets.Various
algorithms,includingtheRandomForestClassifier(RFC),DecisionTree
Classifier (DTC), Support Vector Machines (SVM), AdaBoost Classifier
(ADB), andCatBoost Classifier (CBC),were used to trainthemodels on
thetrainingset.Thetrainedmodelswerethenusedtomakepredictions
on the test set. After generating predictions, the performance of each
model was evaluated by comparing the predicted ripeness stages with
the actual labels from the test set. This evaluation provided valuable
insights into the effectiveness and performance characteristics of each
model, enabling informed decisions regarding their deployment in
practical applications. To ensure a comprehensive evaluation of the
machine learning models utilized in this study, detailed parameter set-
tings and training procedures for each algorithm are essential. The
configuration parameters for the ML algorithms considered are given
below.
• Random Forest Classifier (RFC): The model was configured with 100
estimators and a random state of 42 to ensure reproducibility. The
RFC was trained on the normalized training dataset, and its perfor-
mance was assessed using accuracy metrics on the test set.
• Decision Tree Classifier (DTC):Itwassetwitharandomstateof21to
facilitateconsistentresults.Thetraininginvolvedfittingthemodelto
the normalized data, with performance evaluated based on test set
predictions compared to actual labels.
• K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm:Themodelwasconfiguredwith
5 neighbours, a choice that balances sensitivity and specificity. The
KNN model was trained on the normalized dataset, and its effec-
tiveness was measured through predictions on the test set.
• Support Vector Machine (SVM): The model was configured with a
random state of 21 to maintain consistency. The training involved
fitting the model to the normalized training data, and performance
was gauged based on its predictions on the test set.
• CatBoost Classifier (CBC): It underwent a rigorous hyperparameter
optimization process using Optuna. Initial settings included a
random seed of 21. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, depth,
colsample_bylevel, min_data_in_leaf, and bootstrap_type were opti-
mized.Thelearningraterangedfrom1e-3to0.1,depthfrom1to10,
colsample_bylevel from 0.05 to 1.0, and min_data_in_leaf from 1 to
100, with bootstrap_type selected from ’Bernoulli’ and ’MVS’. The
subsample parameter was optimized when bootstrap_type was not
’Bayesian’. The model was trained with the best-found hyper-
parameters, and accuracy was evaluated on the test set.AdaBoost
Classifier (ABC):Itwasconfiguredwith50boostingiterationsanda
learning rate of 0.005. The model was trained on the normalized

Data analysis was performed using the appropriate statistical

humidity, TVOC, ethanol, and other volatile compounds—and the ba-

• Temperature: As bananas ripen, their metabolic rate increases,
leadingtohigherrespirationandethyleneproduction,whichinturn
affects the temperature of the fruit. Studies have shown that tem-
perature significantly impacts the ripening speed and quality of ba-
nanas. For instance, elevated temperatures can accelerate ripening,
leading to faster colour change and texture softening.
• Humidity: Humidity levels influence the rate of moisture loss from
bananas, affecting their texture and shelf life. High humidity can
slowdowntheripeningprocessbyreducingtherateofmoistureloss,
whilelowhumiditycanleadtoprematuredehydrationandspoilage

In conclusion, the results of our study demonstrate the promising
potential of integrating Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning
(ML) technologies in automating fruit ripeness assessment. Our pro-
posed framework, which employed various ML algorithms, found that

DevelopinganIoTandML-drivenplatformforfruitripenessevaluationand
spoilage detection: A case study on bananas
Rajini Ma,*, Persis Voolab
a Department of CSE, Government Degree College, Ravulapalem, A.P, India
b Department of CSE, Adikavi Nannaya University, Rajahmundry, A.P, India
ARTICLE INFO
Keywords:
Internet of Things
Cold chain
Fruit quality prediction
CatBoost classifier
ABSTRACT
Food waste is a significant global problem that demands immediate action to reduce it. This study presents a
novel framework that merges Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) technologies to detect fruit
ripenessandspoilage,whichisessentialinminimizinglossesinthecoldchainprocessoffreshproduceindustry.
The study employed temperature, humidity, and gas emission sensors along with an ESP32 microcontroller to
establish a unique framework that achieved exceptional accuracy in predicting banana ripeness stages. This
framework employedvarious machinelearning algorithmstodetect ripenessstages, with theCatBoost classifier
exhibiting exceptional performance, demonstrating its dependability and effectiveness in assessing fruit quality.
Thebenefitsofthisresearchextendbeyondfruitripenessdetectionandpavethewayforfutureadvancementsin
automating quality assessment in agricultural supply chains.
1. Introduction
Food waste is a pressing problem globally and in India, which pre-
sentssignificantenvironmentalandsocioeconomicchallenges.InIndia,
withitsgrowingurbanizationandpopulation,approximately1.3billion
tonnes of food is wasted annually. That amounts to the produce of
approximately28%ofthecountry’stotalagriculturalland.EachIndian
citizen generates 0.5 kg of organic waste daily. The United Nations Sus-
tainable Development Goal 12.3aimstohalveglobalfoodwasteby2030,
acknowledging its detrimental impact on land, water, energy, and
greenhouse gas emissions [1,2]. An estimated 40–50 % of the world’s
fruits and vegetables are lost or wasted throughout the supply chain,
accounting for approximately half of all food waste [2]. This leads to a
waste of resources, unnecessary greenhouse gas emissions, and sub-
stantialeconomicloss[3].Therefore,reducingfoodwasteinthesupply
chainisessentialforbothenvironmentalandeconomicreasons.Various
factors contribute to high losses in the fresh fruit and vegetable sector,
including weather and the lack of alternative markets. Ludwig-Ohm
et al., [4] investigated on strawberries, apples, lettuce, and carrots and
found out that, on average, 25 % of vegetables, 15 % to 20 % of
strawberriesand6%to16%ofapplesarelostatthefarmlevel.Mostof
the food waste is attributed to fruits, vegetables, and grains. But to
reduce losses, precautionary measures like protected cultivation,
continuous cooling, improved packaging, and staff training need to be
considered. Besides that, increased cooperation between growers,

fruit ripeness. This superiority highlighted the dependability and effi-
ciency of our model for advancing the field of fruit quality assessment.
The scope of future research in this area is vast, with opportunities for
explorationandimprovement.Thepotentialoftheframeworktoassess
ripeness stages invarious fruits beyond bananas isworth investigating.
Moreover, optimizing the algorithm and dataset can lead to increased
accuracy and more versatile applications for fruit ripeness evaluation.
Thisresearchlaysthefoundationforcontinuedadvancementsintheuse
of IoT and ML technologies for automating fruit ripeness assessment.

ABSTRACT
Food waste is a significant global problem that demands immediate action to reduce it. This study presents a
novel framework that merges Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) technologies to detect fruit
ripenessandspoilage,whichisessentialinminimizinglossesinthecoldchainprocessoffreshproduceindustry.
The study employed temperature, humidity, and gas emission sensors along with an ESP32 microcontroller to
establish a unique framework that achieved exceptional accuracy in predicting banana ripeness stages. This
framework employedvarious machinelearning algorithmstodetect ripenessstages, with theCatBoost classifier
exhibiting exceptional performance, demonstrating its dependability and effectiveness in assessing fruit quality.
Thebenefitsofthisresearchextendbeyondfruitripenessdetectionandpavethewayforfutureadvancementsin
automating quality assessment in agricultural supply chains.
1. Introduction
Food waste is a pressing problem globally and in India, which pre-
sentssignificantenvironmentalandsocioeconomicchallenges.InIndia,
withitsgrowingurbanizationandpopulation,approximately1.3billion
tonnes of food is wasted annually. That amounts to the produce of
approximately28%ofthecountry’stotalagriculturalland.EachIndian
citizen generates 0.5 kg of organic waste daily. The United Nations Sus-
tainable Development Goal 12.3aimstohalveglobalfoodwasteby2030,
acknowledging its detrimental impact on land, water, energy, and
greenhouse gas emissions [1,2]. An estimated 40–50 % of the world’s
fruits and vegetables are lost or wasted throughout the supply chain,
accounting for approximately half of all food waste [2]. This leads to a
waste of resources, unnecessary greenhouse gas emissions, and sub-
stantialeconomicloss[3].Therefore,reducingfoodwasteinthesupply
chainisessentialforbothenvironmentalandeconomicreasons.Various
factors contribute to high losses in the fresh fruit and vegetable sector,
including weather and the lack of alternative markets. Ludwig-Ohm
et al., [4] investigated on strawberries, apples, lettuce, and carrots and
found out that, on average, 25 % of vegetables, 15 % to 20 % of
strawberriesand6%to16%ofapplesarelostatthefarmlevel.Mostof
the food waste is attributed to fruits, vegetables, and grains. But to
reduce losses, precautionary measures like protected cultivation,
continuous cooling, improved packaging, and staff training need to be
considered. Besides that, increased cooperation between growers,
wholesalers, and retailers can enhance the marketable product share.
This highlights the importance of the environment in maintaining
freshnessandsafety.Itiscrucialtocontinuouslymonitortheircondition
toensuretheirqualityandnutritionalvalue.Astheconventionalmeans
of tracking the condition of produce in supply chains is outdated and
lackdigitalization,therapidspoilageoftheseitemsnecessitatescareful
storage and transportation to extend their shelf life and preserve their
post-harvestquality[5].Theripenessoffruitsisafundamentalaspectof
agricultural production and supply chain industry. It is a critical deter-
minant of the quality and market value of fruits, impacting both pro-
ducers and consumers. For farmers and producers, accurate and timely
ripeness detection is essential for optimizing harvesting schedules,
reducingpost-harvestlosses,andensuringthatfruitsreachconsumersin
their prime condition. Consumers, on the other hand, rely on the ripe-
ness of fruits to make informed purchasing decisions, seeking produce
thatmeetstheirtastepreferencesandnutritionalrequirements[6].Fruit
ripeness assessment typically relies on visual inspection by skilled
personnel; however, this method is subjective, time-consuming, and
prone to errors due to external factors such as fatigue and bias.
Present study considered banana fruit as India is one of the largest
producers of Banana. Its availability throughout the year made it

cold chain processes, there is large amount of spoilage in banana pro-
duce resulting losses to the farmers as well as producers [7–10]. The
losses are mainly due to lapses in assessing banana ripeness. The con-

TheprimaryaimofthisstudyistopresentanIoTsystemintegrated
with a machine-learning technique for fruit ripeness detection and

The following are the key contributions of this work:
1. This study addresses the pressing global issue of food security and
contributestothereductionoffruitwastebyproposingamethodto
detect fruit freshness or spoilage before it occurs.
2. A novelframeworkwasdevelopedthatharnessesthecapabilitiesof
IoT sensors and machine learning techniques to effectively evaluate
and monitor banana ripeness, offering a practical solution to the
identified problem.
3. The successful integration of two key sensors, namely SHT40 and
SGP30, alongside an ESP32 Development board, is demonstrated as
the core component of the proposed system. These sensors play a
crucial role in capturing emissions from fruits and facilitating the
assessment of their ripeness and overall quality.
4. Through extensive experimentation employing various machine
learningalgorithms,theresearchachievedahighlevelofaccuracyin
classifying sensor data over a one-week period. Notably, the Cat-
Boost classifier stands out for its exceptional accuracy in evaluating
the collected data.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a system that integrates physical ob-
jects and communication technologies to create a networked world
where devices can communicate with each other. Technologies such as
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, radio-frequency identification (RFID), and Wireless
Sensor Networks (WSNs) enable interconnectivity. IoT goes beyond
traditional web browsing and allows remote monitoring and control of
physical environments [11]. The integration of modern technologies,
such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML), offers
thepotentialtorevolutionizetheassessmentoffruitripeness.TheIoT’s
ability to collect real-time data and ML’s capacity to analyse complex
datasets make it possible to develop automated, data-driven solutions
forfruitripenessdetection.Despitenumerousstudiesutilizingadvanced
technologiesforripenessdetection,thereislimitedresearchexamining
the efficacy of these technologies in evaluating fruit ripeness and
spoilage.

inaradicalway.Severalstudiesfocussedonharnessingtheadvantages

The sensor node is the combination of the microcontroller and the

potential of integrating Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning
(ML) technologies in automating fruit ripeness assessment. Our pro-

the CatBoost Classifier achieves high accuracy in predicting banana
ripenessstages.Thisishighwhencomparedtootherstudiesfocusedon
fruit ripeness. This superiority highlighted the dependability and effi-
ciency of our model for advancing the field of fruit quality assessment.
The scope of future research in this area is vast, with opportunities for
explorationandimprovement.Thepotentialoftheframeworktoassess
ripeness stages invarious fruits beyond bananas isworth investigating.
Moreover, optimizing the algorithm and dataset can lead to increased
accuracy and more versatile applications for fruit ripeness evaluation.

Problem Statement ID – 26154

Category – Software

Problem Statement Title

Gen AI Platform for Automated Content Transformation

Description

• Background Organisations frequently need to convert information available in different forms such as news articles, reports, advisories, threat intelligence, policy documents, research papers, announcements, incident reports or free-form prompts into specific communication artefacts suitable for various purposes. The process of manually analysing the source content, understanding the desired objective and creating the required output format is time-consuming, resource-intensive and often requires expertise in content creation, communication and domain knowledge.

There is a need for an intelligent platform that can transform user-provided content into a desired output format through a simple and configurable interface.
• Description The system shall act as an AI-powered content transformation engine that converts a common source of information into the specific deliverable requested by the operator, thereby reducing manual effort, improving consistency, accelerating content creation and enhancing operational efficiency.

The platform shall provide a dashboard through which an operator can submit source content in the form of high quality English language text, documents, articles, reports, prompts, images, videos or contextual information. In addition to providing the source content, the operator shall select one or more desired output types through configurable parameters available on the dashboard.

Based on the submitted content and the selected output type(s), the platform shall analyze the input, understand the context and intent, and generate the requested output artefact. The platform should support multiple output formats and allow operators to control generation parameters such as target audience, tone, language, level of detail, communication objective and content style.

In sum

mary, platform shall generate output corresponding to the option(s) selected by the operator on the dashboard.
• Examples include
• If 'Video' is selected, generate a complete video package including script, storyboard, scene descriptions, narration text, subtitles and visual recommendations.
• If 'LinkedIn Post' is selected, generate a professional LinkedIn post suitable for publication.
• If 'Twitter/X Post' is selected, generate platform-optimized tweets or tweet threads.
• If 'Advisory' is selected, generate a structured advisory document.
• If 'Infographic' is selected, generate infographic content, layout recommendations and key messaging.
• If 'Executive Summary' is selected, generate a concise executive briefing.
• If 'Presentation' is selected, generate presentation slides and speaker notes.
• If multiple output formats are selected, generate all selected deliverables from the same source content.
• Expected Solution/Deliverables for Evaluation
• Source Code Link (GitHub/Drive Link)
• Readme with Setup Instructions
• Architecture Document (Max 2 Pages)
• Demo Video (Max 2 Minutes)
• Technical Presentation (Max 5 Slides)
